title: Lapse of a Home Mortgage Loans Application Not Closed Within the Funding Window
content:
An application for a Home Mortgage Loans note that has not closed is withdrawn once the program's funding window in calendar days has passed after the application was recorded.

## How the days are counted

Calendar days are counted with the day after the date the application was recorded as day 1. The application lapses when the current date is on or after the date the application was recorded plus the program's funding window in calendar days. The date the application was recorded is held in the bank's own record of that application, and it is that record, and not a date the borrower recalls, that anchors the count.

## Both sides of the boundary

Take a hypothetical application on a program whose funding window is 60 calendar days, recorded on a given date and still not closed.

- On the sixtieth day after the date it was recorded, the current date has reached the date it was recorded plus 60 calendar days. The comparison is satisfied on that day as well as on any later one, so the application has lapsed.
- On the fifty-ninth day after the date it was recorded, the current date has not yet reached that date, so the application has not lapsed.

The same reading applies to a program whose funding window is longer: the lapse falls on the day equal to the date the application was recorded plus that program's own number of calendar days, and not before.

## Basis of judgement

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | The application being recorded |
| Verifiable record | The application's recorded date, in the bank's records |
| Counting | Calendar days, the day after the recorded date being day 1 |
| Direction of the comparison | The current date is not earlier than the recorded date plus the window |
| The boundary day itself | Counts as lapsed |
| Result | The application is withdrawn |
